evidence: Source reads/edits and cached Java classes decoded as data only; no class loading, builds, tests, syntax checks, JNI/project/game execution, shader/GPU execution or Bedrock operations

reference.normal: PlayerModel constructor selects RenderTypes.entityTranslucent; LivingEntityRenderer.getRenderType uses model.renderType for the visible-body branch
reference.otherBranches: LivingEntityRenderer separately selects entityTranslucentCullItemTarget for the translucent-invisible branch, outline for the outline branch, or no material
reference.ghostSelection: Cached LivingEntityRenderer.submit sets translucent-invisible when !isBodyVisible(state) && !state.isInvisibleToPlayer; getRenderType prioritizes this branch, then visible model.renderType, then appearsGlowing outline, then null. Entity invisibility alone cannot select it.
reference.ghostTint: LivingEntityRenderer.submit selects integer 654311423 (0x26ffffff) for the translucent-invisible branch and -1 (0xffffffff) otherwise, then calls ARGB.multiply with getModelTint(state) before submitModel. Neither a floating alpha of 0.15 nor native skin fade establishes this selected vertex color.
reference.ghostTarget: Cached RenderTypes.lambda$static$9 constructs entity_translucent_cull_item_target using ENTITY_TRANSLUCENT_CULL and explicitly OutputTarget.ITEM_ENTITY_TARGET, lightmap, overlay, sortOnUpload and AFFECTS_OUTLINE. It must not be aliased to the visible skin's main output target or an arbitrary same-size native render target.
reference.ghostPipeline: Cached RenderPipelines.<clinit> 007ed..00822 builds ENTITY_TRANSLUCENT_CULL from ENTITY_SNIPPET with ALPHA_CUTOUT float 0.1 and TRANSLUCENT color blending. ENTITY_SNIPPET 000d3..00106 supplies entity shaders, SAMPLER0_SAMPLER2, ENTITY vertices, QUADS and DepthStencilState.DEFAULT; cached DEFAULT 00000..0000b selects GREATER_THAN_OR_EQUAL and depth writes. Unlike the ordinary entityTranslucent pipeline, the cull builder does not disable culling or add PER_FACE_LIGHTING; the remaining builder cull default and separate item-entity target still need their own implementation/ownership join.
reference.overlay: entity.fsh applies the selected overlay texel before the lightmap; Arctic's custom cosmetic PoseXform uses NO_OVERLAY separately

input.class: Immutable JavaSkinMaterial with explicit entityTranslucent factory and copied normalized RGBA overlay
input.snapshot: WorldFrame.Player.javaSkinMaterial: schema 1, kind entity-translucent, overlayColor four normalized floats; declared world coordinate space required
input.selection: No material is inferred from image alpha or the cosmetic overlay. Missing selection retains GENERAL staging, which native material preparation still rejects.
input.scope: Adapter-owned target-Java inputs; this field is not an installed-game capture or suppression receipt

rendering.sharedEmitter: Only normal JavaPlayerMesh parts use skinSink; bent SkinLimbs remain in the Arctic cosmetic pass after worn models
rendering.software: Explicit JAVA_SKIN pass has .1 sampled-alpha cutout, per-face lighting, translucency and depth writes; its own overlay is emitted per vertex and survives homogeneous clipping and perspective interpolation (entity-overlay-varying-source.json)
rendering.native: SkinTranslucent role shares the entity-translucent GPU state with cosmetic base, while retaining a separate semantic kind and per-batch selected texel emitted through the smooth shader overlay varying
rendering.constants: Inputs.for_batch selects the skin overlay; frame-only skin preparation rejects. Constant preparation checks copied overlay bytes even for low-level explicit input, plus all copied shader/lightmap bytes when present.
rendering.sortIdentity: The order planner permits the two entityTranslucent roles to share an adapter-proven prepared identity. It still requires caller-supplied object/equality/group IDs, matching texture and sorting; it does not infer them.

wire.magic: ARCGEO03 base layout; ARCGEO04 adds skin visibility provenance and bent-skin role (skin-visibility-source.json)
wire.header: Same optional material flag and 1058-float cohort as ARCGEO02
wire.batch: Same 32-byte fixed batch header; pass 6 appends four normalized finite f32 overlay components before vertices, including for empty submits
wire.compatibility: Decoder retains ARCGEO01..04. Pass 6 requires v3+, and native preparation now requires v4 supplied-visibility knowledge for skin. Existing 96 MiB and topology bounds include the extension.

replay.track: bedrock_body_samples_v6 appends visibility after the retained v5 material field
replay.actorExtension: After the v4 optional packed light: u8 0 unknown or 1 entityTranslucent, followed for 1 by four normalized f32 overlay components
replay.ownership: BodySample retains immutable material selection; copying and equality preserve it
replay.sampling: Exact endpoints preserve selection. Interior samples preserve it only when both selections/overlays agree; changing or missing values remain unknown.
replay.legacy: V1-v4 retain unknown skin material; v5 retains its material without fabricated v6 visibility
replay.playback: Uses recorded selection rather than live viewer metadata; body appearance readiness requires a known selection, and missing v5 selections prevent new body plans
